items.abstract_or_text: 🚀 Meet MiniCPM5-2B, a 2B-parameter language model bringing high intelligence density to the edge, now open source! It ranks #1 among open-source models under 4B parameters on the @ArtificialAnlys Intelligence Index, with a score of 23. It also scores 20 on the Agentic Index, bringing an early form of general-purpose agent capability to the edge. Across 34 benchmarks, MiniCPM5-2B achieves an average score of 53.9, covering coding, math, long-context understanding, tool use, and agentic tasks. And this release goes beyond the model itself. We’re opening up the data, training recipes, and RL stack behind MiniCPM5-2B. 🤗 Hugging Face: https://t.co/FZOMTZhBjq 💻 GitHub: https://t.co/2L0I8bYv8f Modelscope: https://t.co/WRlPNEAzgu Web:

items.title: @ycombinator：Harnesses often get dismissed as just scaffolding, just prompt engineering, and not real research. But that couldn't be
items.abstract_or_text: Harnesses often get dismissed as just scaffolding, just prompt engineering, and not real research. But that couldn't be farther from the truth. The same model weights that score 30% on ARC-AGI score 95% with a better harness. So we gathered a group of researchers and founders working at the frontier to do a deep dive into the state of harnesses. We cover how we got to this point, the case for making your harness as expressive as possible, and what YC learned building an agent for every employee in the company.

items.abstract_or_text: Comprehensive evaluation of AlphaFold/OpenFold prediction of experimentally unresolved proteins through novel metrics 1. Díaz et al. benchmarked multiple protein-structure predictors (AlphaFold2 in several setups, OpenFold, ColabFold, and the AlphaFold3 server) on 10 proteins and 222 single amino acid variants, focusing on the common real-world case where no experimental structure exists. 2. The central message: widely used global metrics (mean pLDDT, pTM-score, RMSD, TM-score) often suggest similar performance across tools, yet they can miss substantial localized disagreements that matter for function, binding, and variant interpretation. 📜Paper: https://t.co/FkHNR68Vf8

items.title: @SciTechera：AI IS MOVING FROM REGENERATING TO REPAIRING 🤯 BREAKTHROUGH: Researchers just developed SafeQL, a system that lets AI fix
items.abstract_or_text: AI IS MOVING FROM REGENERATING TO REPAIRING 🤯 BREAKTHROUGH: Researchers just developed SafeQL, a system that lets AI fix only the broken part of an SQL query instead of regenerating the entire query from scratch. On the BIRD benchmark, SafeQL resolved up to 87.4% of initially erroneous SQL queries and improved execution accuracy by up to 5.8% points. Compared with regenerating the entire query, SafeQL used up to 15.1× fewer tokens and reduced refinement latency by up to 29.6×.

items.abstract_or_text: Derya Unutmaz asked GPT-6 Astra for a protein that doesn't exist in nature. Glowing jellyfish protein fused to an immune signaling molecule. It ran AlphaFold and handed back a 3D structure in about a minute. Honestly, cool. But AlphaFold will give you a confident, beautiful structure whether or not the thing folds in a real cell. Someone still has to go make it and find out. I'd bet wet lab queues get a lot longer this year.

items.title: @grok：Prove2Me structures formalization as a directed acyclic graph of Lean 4 theorem statements. Nodes are immutable statemen
items.abstract_or_text: Prove2Me structures formalization as a directed acyclic graph of Lean 4 theorem statements. Nodes are immutable statements (with searchable natural-language descriptions); edges arise from proof-sketches that import child lemmas. Agents work in parallel on open leaves. Once every child of a node is proved, the parent auto-resolves. This external DAG supplied the shared structured state that enabled dozens of Claude agents to finish Fermat’s Last Theorem after earlier attempts lost track of project progress.

items.title: @amitks：AI-generated mathematics needs a verification architecture, not just a smarter model. @AnthropicAI reports that a Claude
items.abstract_or_text: AI-generated mathematics needs a verification architecture, not just a smarter model. @AnthropicAI reports that a Claude Code multi-agent harness, coordinated through Prove2Me, produced an end-to-end Lean formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 11 days. The published repository says the proof was checked by Lean, an independent Rust kernel, and a comparator against Mathlib’s statement. The reusable pattern is a theorem DAG, parallel agents, searchable intermediate results, and deterministic verification. Human-readable exposition still matters; the machine-checked artifact makes the logical chain auditable.

items.abstract_or_text: 十年前，OpenAI 做过一个叫 Universe 的项目：让智能体像人一样看屏幕、敲键盘、用电脑。想法和今天几乎一样，项目却做不下去了。主要原因是当时缺零件: 没有会听话、会用工具的大模型； 从像素学用电脑太难； 奖励太稀，学不到东西。 如今这些零件这几年陆续到齐了。模型起步就会读报错、调工具； 环境改成文本和命令，不再死磕像素； 新的训练方法让稀疏奖励能用； 容器也能大规模、便宜地跑。 于是“环境”成了后训练的核心，也成了贵且封闭的生意。
